bull_bear.body: Prioritizing organic growth via referrals and institutional partnerships; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; strong cash position enables future M&A or content development if regulatory shift occurs
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Regulatory risk if UGC restricts third-party content development; over-reliance on institutional partners; execution risk in scaling J.K. Shah partnership; potential margin pressure if CAC rises due to new market entry
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, disciplined, bootstrapped mindset; emphasis on profitability over growth-at-all-costs; proud of 17-year track record of consistent profits and zero cash burn; tone is founder-led, human-capital-centric
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: 35-36% of new enrollments come from learner referrals — a rare, defensible moat in EdTech; Jaro’s studios are embedded inside IIM campuses, creating institutional lock-in; Jio partnership gives free access to 100M+ Jio Fiber users — a stealth distribution channel
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Model is asset-light with revenue recognised "over program lifecycle with strong visibility", and surplus "Reinvest[ed] to scale and strengthen capabilities" per the growth-loop slide.
- The FY26 snapshot footnote states: "ROCE & ROE decreased due to an increase in share capital following the IPO in September 2025 (FY25: ROCE: 33%, ROE: 35%)" — the FY25 comparatives are quoted; the FY26 ROCE/ROE values could not be reliably bound to their labels in this extract.
- Finance cost fell sharply in Q1 FY27 (15.98 Lakhs vs 149.24 Lakhs in Q1 FY26), consistent with the post-IPO balance sheet, though the deck offers no debt or net-cash disclosure.
- No dividend policy, buyback, IPO proceeds utilisation or acquisition plan is disclosed in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- distribution: Partnership network spans 33 Partner Institutions including 7 IIMs and 5 IITs and 19 Tier-2 universities and institutions and 2 Global Institutes as of March 31, 2026 — evidence: Directors' Report states partnerships with 33 Partner Institutions (7 IIMs, 5 IITs, 19 Tier-2 universities/institutions, 2 Global Institutes).
- customer lock-in: Programme-level exclusivity with certain partner institutions — evidence: Symbiosis International's online programmes are offered exclusively through Jaro Education, per the Corporate Overview.
- cost position: Asset-light, partner-led model requiring no company capital expenditure to capture rising higher-education spend — evidence: MD&A states the Company operates an asset light, partner led model without the need to deploy its own capital expenditure, and its balance sheet remains near debt free.
- distribution: Fee-collection custodian role for a large share of partner institutions — evidence: Corporate Overview states Jaro acts as fee-collection custodian for 47% of Partner Institutions, remitting fees on their behalf.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Intensifying competition in the online higher education and upskilling segment — Management flags this may affect pricing, learner acquisition cost and market share.
- Dependence on partner universities retaining valid UGC / AICTE / ODL approvals — Loss of approval at a partner institution would directly affect the programmes the Company can offer through that partner.
- Regulatory risk in the UGC framework — Changes in the UGC framework, or in the entitlements of partner institutions, could affect the Company's ability to offer certain programmes.
- Concentration of revenue in degree programmes — Exposes the Company to programme-specific and partner-specific factors.
- Sensitivity of enrolments to marketing and brand-building expenditure — Enrolments are sensitive to the quantum and timing of marketing and brand-building spend.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Corporate upskilling (IITs/IIMs/Symbiosis): 30% higher fee programs (INR2-9L); J.K. Shah commerce vertical: 4.2M TAM, online-only, same margin as peers; Jio ecosystem: free access via set-top boxes; School Connect (IIT Madras): new vertical targeting school children
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- "Founded in 2009, Jaro Education is an early and established edtech player in India, focused on expanding access to quality higher education and professional upskilling beyond traditional campuses."
- Acts as "an end-to-end enabler, managing the complete programme lifecycle from admissions and learner outreach to technology-enabled delivery, bridging institutions and learners at scale" — a fee-sharing model rather than a degree-granting one.
- "Why Jaro Wins" rests on four claims: deep institutional partnerships enabling "program co-creation", business intelligence on learner demand, an integrated platform across "program design, acquisition, and delivery", and proven revenue generation for partner institutions via a dedicated sales team.
- Investment case is stated as "Scalable, asset-light model", "Favorable unit economics", "Operating leverage driving margin expansion", "Strong revenue visibility with long-duration programs" and "Recession free industry".
- Growth is described as a self-reinforcing loop: partnerships → business intelligence → portfolio expansion → sales/counselling engine → learner acquisition → revenue share reinvested "to scale and strengthen capabilities".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [IPO] The deck references an IPO in September 2025 as the reason for the increased share capital; "Current Market Cap (as on 10th Aug 2026)" is shown alongside a figure of 1,023 Cr. in the same snapshot block.
- [Ecosystem] Partnered with ET Education as E-learning Partner for the 3rd ET Education Annual Education Summit 2026 (12 June 2026) and participated in the panel "Education to Economy: Powering India's $5 Trillion Future".
- [Milestone] "17 YEARS OF IMPACT, INNOVATION & INSPIRATION" — the company dates its journey "From a bold vision in 2009".
- [IR] Investor relations is outsourced to SAAA Consultants Pvt. Ltd.; Chairman & MD is Dr. Sanjay Salunkhe, CEO & Wholetime Director Ranjita Raman (with Jaro since 2010, IIM Ahmedabad alumna) and CFO Sankesh Mophe (since 2011, founding member).

business.body: Jaro Institute of Technology Management and Research Limited provides programme management and enrolment facilitation services in partnership with universities and academic institutions, operating in India's online higher education and professional upskilling sector. It markets and facilitates delivery of a diversified range of online degree programmes (MBA, M.Com, M.A, PGDM, M.C.A, M.Sc, B.Com, BCA) and cross-disciplinary certification courses in partnership with institutions, and is also developing a corporate (B2B) learning vertical launched in FY26.

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin improved to 26.12% (9M) due to reduced CAC via 35-36% referral rate; marketing spend optimized; fixed cost leverage from 17 studios; ARPU doubling (INR43k→84k) driven by shift to higher fee programs (30% of mix)
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 20-25% FY26; margin: targeting EBITDA >30%, PAT >19-20%; order inflow: no explicit target, but J.K. Shah partnership to drive volume from April; capex/commissioning: 17 studios already deployed, no new capex guidance
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Expansion into Tier 2/3 cities (Kolkata, Indore); J.K. Shah partnership (4.2M commerce learners); potential entry into content development if UGC permits; School Connect vertical for K-12; Jio ecosystem reach
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Scale up the corporate (B2B) learning vertical, launched during FY26, to diversify revenue beyond individual learners by expanding the enterprise client base and deepening engagement with existing corporate partners.
- Invest in AI-driven capabilities across the learner lifecycle (programme discovery, counselling, engagement, support) to improve conversion, enhance learner experience and strengthen operating efficiency, partly funded by unutilised IPO proceeds earmarked for marketing and technology.
- Strengthen and deepen academic partnerships, including expanding the portfolio of industry-aligned and AI-linked programmes with leading Tier-1 institutions.
- Continue a multi-year shift of the programme mix toward shorter certification formats alongside full degree programmes, aligned with the industry move toward working-professional upskilling.
- Extend distribution reach into Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets through technology and consumer-platform tie-ups, extending access beyond metropolitan centres.
outlook.title: Strategy

outlook.body: The Company operates an asset-light, partner-led model and states it has no need to deploy its own capital expenditure to capture rising higher-education spend; partner institutions expand seats and programmes funded by their own budgets. Expansion is instead described in terms of the corporate (B2B) learning vertical launched in FY26 (in an early stage), continued growth of the academic-partner network, and distribution reach into Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets through technology and consumer-platform tie-ups.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand is shaped by India's higher-education policy framework, particularly NEP 2020's target of raising the Gross Enrolment Ratio to 50% by 2035 (from approximately 28.4% per AISHE 2021-22), acting as a catalyst for online education.
- India's demographic profile — a median age of approximately 29 years and a working-age (15-64) population of roughly 68%, the largest such cohort globally — is expected to sustain demand for executive education and professional upskilling over the medium term.
- The Union Budget 2026-27 raised the higher-education allocation and included initiatives (Centre of Excellence in AI in Education, industry corridor University Townships, AVGC Content Creator Labs) that management says reinforce demand for employability-focused, AI-led, industry-aligned programmes.
- Government policy tailwinds — NEP 2020 emphasis on ODL/online formats and vocational, industry-aligned skilling, and the proposed University Townships — are cited as opportunities.
- A policy focus on AI, digital technologies and future-of-work skills is cited as an opportunity area, with the Company noting more than 12 programmes incorporating AI, machine learning and Generative AI in the curriculum.
- Expansion of the corporate/B2B learning vertical is cited as addressing enterprise workforce upskilling demand and broadening the revenue base beyond individual learners.
- Gross bookings, representing committed enrolments, are cited by management as a leading indicator providing visibility into the forward revenue pipeline.
- Risks flagged by management include intensifying competition affecting pricing, learner acquisition cost and market share; dependence on partner universities retaining valid UGC/AICTE/ODL approvals; regulatory risk from changes in the UGC framework; revenue concentration in degree programmes; and sensitivity of enrolments to the quantum and timing of marketing/brand-building expenditure.
- Gross bookings, representing committed enrolments, are cited as a leading indicator of revenue to be recognised in subsequent periods and provide visibility into the forward revenue pipeline; the Company states it remains focused on converting this pipeline efficiently while managing learner-acquisition costs.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Jaro delivered strong Q3FY26 execution with 42% YoY revenue growth and EBITDA profitability after prior losses, driven by higher ARPU (up 2x in 4 years), referral-led customer acquisition (35-36%), and strategic partnerships with IITs/IIMs; what matters is the sustainable margin trajectory (EBITDA 26% for 9M) and scalable model without cash burn, positioning it as India’s only consistently profitable EdTech platform.

open.item: The Company is prioritising the scale-up of its corporate (B2B) learning vertical, launched during FY26, to expand its enterprise client base and deepen engagement with existing corporate partners.

The Company is investing in AI-driven capabilities across the learner lifecycle to improve conversion, enhance learner experience and strengthen operating efficiency, supported in part by unutilised IPO proceeds earmarked for marketing and technology.
The unutilised balance of the IPO net proceeds, held in monitoring/permitted instruments as at March 31, 2026, would be spent in FY27 to fund the Company's growth.
The Company will continue to strengthen and deepen its academic partnerships, including expanding its portfolio of industry-aligned and AI-linked programmes with leading Tier-1 institutions.
The Company intends to expand its enterprise client base and deepen engagement with existing corporate partners over the coming year as part of scaling up the corporate (B2B) learning vertical.
The Company is extending distribution reach into Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets through technology and consumer-platform tie-ups, extending access beyond metropolitan centres.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Jaro Education is an asset-light programme-management and enrolment-facilitation company connecting learners with partner universities and academic institutions for online higher education and professional upskilling.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Jaro Institute of Technology Management and Research Limited provides programme management and enrolment facilitation services in partnership with universities and academic institutions, operating in India's online higher education and professional upskilling sector. It markets and facilitates delivery of a diversified range of online degree programmes (MBA, M.Com, M.A, PGDM, M.C.A, M.Sc, B.Com, BCA) and cross-disciplinary certification courses in partnership with institutions, and is also developing a corporate (B2B) learning vertical launched in FY26.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand is shaped by India's higher-education policy framework, particularly NEP 2020's target of raising the Gross Enrolment Ratio to 50% by 2035 (from approximately 28.4% per AISHE 2021-22), acting as a catalyst for online education.
- India's demographic profile — a median age of approximately 29 years and a working-age (15-64) population of roughly 68%, the largest such cohort globally — is expected to sustain demand for executive education and professional upskilling over the medium term.
- The Union Budget 2026-27 raised the higher-education allocation and included initiatives (Centre of Excellence in AI in Education, industry corridor University Townships, AVGC Content Creator Labs) that management says reinforce demand for employability-focused, AI-led, industry-aligned programmes.
- Government policy tailwinds — NEP 2020 emphasis on ODL/online formats and vocational, industry-aligned skilling, and the proposed University Townships — are cited as opportunities.
- A policy focus on AI, digital technologies and future-of-work skills is cited as an opportunity area, with the Company noting more than 12 programmes incorporating AI, machine learning and Generative AI in the curriculum.
- Expansion of the corporate/B2B learning vertical is cited as addressing enterprise workforce upskilling demand and broadening the revenue base beyond individual learners.
- Gross bookings, representing committed enrolments, are cited by management as a leading indicator providing visibility into the forward revenue pipeline.
- Risks flagged by management include intensifying competition affecting pricing, learner acquisition cost and market share; dependence on partner universities retaining valid UGC/AICTE/ODL approvals; regulatory risk from changes in the UGC framework; revenue concentration in degree programmes; and sensitivity of enrolments to the quantum and timing of marketing/brand-building expenditure.
- Gross bookings, representing committed enrolments, are cited as a leading indicator of revenue to be recognised in subsequent periods and provide visibility into the forward revenue pipeline; the Company states it remains focused on converting this pipeline efficiently while managing learner-acquisition costs.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- distribution: Partnership network spans 33 Partner Institutions including 7 IIMs and 5 IITs and 19 Tier-2 universities and institutions and 2 Global Institutes as of March 31, 2026 — evidence: Directors' Report states partnerships with 33 Partner Institutions (7 IIMs, 5 IITs, 19 Tier-2 universities/institutions, 2 Global Institutes).
- customer lock-in: Programme-level exclusivity with certain partner institutions — evidence: Symbiosis International's online programmes are offered exclusively through Jaro Education, per the Corporate Overview.
- cost position: Asset-light, partner-led model requiring no company capital expenditure to capture rising higher-education spend — evidence: MD&A states the Company operates an asset light, partner led model without the need to deploy its own capital expenditure, and its balance sheet remains near debt free.
- distribution: Fee-collection custodian role for a large share of partner institutions — evidence: Corporate Overview states Jaro acts as fee-collection custodian for 47% of Partner Institutions, remitting fees on their behalf.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Regulatory risk if UGC restricts third-party content development; over-reliance on institutional partners; execution risk in scaling J.K. Shah partnership; potential margin pressure if CAC rises due to new market entry

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: 35-36% of new enrollments come from learner referrals — a rare, defensible moat in EdTech; Jaro’s studios are embedded inside IIM campuses, creating institutional lock-in; Jio partnership gives free access to 100M+ Jio Fiber users — a stealth distribution channel

strategy.title: Strategy
strategy.body:
- Scale up the corporate (B2B) learning vertical, launched during FY26, to diversify revenue beyond individual learners by expanding the enterprise client base and deepening engagement with existing corporate partners.
- Invest in AI-driven capabilities across the learner lifecycle (programme discovery, counselling, engagement, support) to improve conversion, enhance learner experience and strengthen operating efficiency, partly funded by unutilised IPO proceeds earmarked for marketing and technology.
- Strengthen and deepen academic partnerships, including expanding the portfolio of industry-aligned and AI-linked programmes with leading Tier-1 institutions.
- Continue a multi-year shift of the programme mix toward shorter certification formats alongside full degree programmes, aligned with the industry move toward working-professional upskilling.
- Extend distribution reach into Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets through technology and consumer-platform tie-ups, extending access beyond metropolitan centres.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [IPO] The deck references an IPO in September 2025 as the reason for the increased share capital; "Current Market Cap (as on 10th Aug 2026)" is shown alongside a figure of 1,023 Cr. in the same snapshot block.
- [Ecosystem] Partnered with ET Education as E-learning Partner for the 3rd ET Education Annual Education Summit 2026 (12 June 2026) and participated in the panel "Education to Economy: Powering India's $5 Trillion Future".
- [Milestone] "17 YEARS OF IMPACT, INNOVATION & INSPIRATION" — the company dates its journey "From a bold vision in 2009".
- [IR] Investor relations is outsourced to SAAA Consultants Pvt. Ltd.; Chairman & MD is Dr. Sanjay Salunkhe, CEO & Wholetime Director Ranjita Raman (with Jaro since 2010, IIM Ahmedabad alumna) and CFO Sankesh Mophe (since 2011, founding member).
